results.fact: distance: dist_km is one-way, itinerary miles is round trip
results.evidence: dist_km is the one-way approach (0.8 mi, matching the summit waypoint distMi and the overview) and itinerary miles are per day (1.6 mi out and back); 0.8 x 2 = 1.6, so the two quantities agree by the stated convention.

results.fact: access.fees claims no fee; access.passRequired states an explicit dollar fee
results.evidence: Northwest Forest Pass pricing ($5/day, $30/year) and its requirement at developed MBS trailheads is confirmed by the forest's passes page. No source found says the undeveloped FR6517 roadside pull-off (no trail, no facilities) is a posted fee site, so it is not settled whether passRequired's 'required at the FR6517 trailhead parking' is right or whether fees' 'None' should stand; parking_pass and the permit column both limit the pass to developed trailheads. Needs a ranger-district confirmation before either field is changed.

results.fact: Wilderness permit: permit column says a free self-issue Wild Sky Wilderness permit/registration; access.permit says 'None required'
results.evidence: The permit column and access.permit disagree about whether a free self-issue wilderness permit applies. Wild Sky Wilderness has an Eagle Rock unit, but it was not established whether this summit lies inside the designated wilderness or whether a self-issue permit is required there; the relevant pages (Mountaineers, SummitPost) were not readable. Also note access.overnight_permit describes Lake Serene/Barclay Lake, not this route.

The route page's consensus grade is 5.11b (37 votes), matching rock_grade, overview and pitch_detail; but a topo photo on the same site labels it 5.11c, which is likely the original/guidebook grade that `grade` carries. No second independent source settles 5.11b vs 5.11c, and only three row fields agree on 5.11b (grade_num is derived), so the internal-plus-one threshold is not met.

results.fact: Overall route grade (5.10c) vs the grades its own pitches are given
results.evidence: An unlettered '5.10' pitch grade spans 5.10a-d, so a 5.10c overall grade with a '5.10' second pitch is consistent. The route page gives exactly this: overall 5.10c, P1 5.10-, P2 5.10, 13 bolts, FA Windham/Wolfe Sept 2005.

results.fact: Rope length needed to lower off (30 m rope vs a stated 60 m requirement)
results.evidence: The route is a single 60 ft (18 m) pitch with a chain anchor at the top, per its route page; lowering from an 18 m anchor needs well over 36 m of rope, so a 30 m rope cannot reach the ground. length_m (18), pitch length in rappels (~60 ft lower), descent (single rope) and descent_text (single 60 m rope) all agree against rope_length_m=30.

results.fact: Rope length needed to lower off (30 m rope vs a stated 60 m requirement)
results.correct_value: Lower with a single rope (a 30 m rope suffices for the 12 m pitch)
results.evidence: The route page gives a 40 ft (12 m) pitch with 4 bolts and a chain anchor, so any single rope of 30 m or more lowers it. length_m (12), pitch_detail lengthM (12), rappels (~40 ft), descent ('single rope') and rope_length_m (30) agree; descent_text's '60m' is the lone outlier and is removed so the rope stated is not contradicted.

patches.find: to the ground with a single 60m rope;
patches.replace: to the ground with a single rope (30 m is enough for this 12 m pitch);

results.fact: Overall route grade (5.10b) vs the grades its own pitches are given
results.evidence: '5.10-' conventionally denotes the lower half of 5.10 (a/b), so a 5.10b overall grade is consistent with a 5.10- first pitch. The route page gives exactly this: overall 5.10b, P1 5.10- (60 ft), P2 5.9- (60 ft), 13 bolts, gear to 2 in.

results.fact: rappels field says 0 while descent_text describes a possible rappel
results.evidence: descent_text says there is no established rappel line and frames the single short rappel as an optional contingency off a party-built anchor; rappels '0' states the standard count of required rappels. The two agree that no rappel is part of the route.

results.fact: dist_km appears one-way while itinerary total is round-trip, presented as the same 'distance'
results.evidence: dist_km is the one-way figure by convention (23.35 km = 14.5 mi = 11.5 mi to Cub Lake + half of the 6 mi summit day) and itinerary miles are per day totalling 29 mi round trip; they agree.

results.correct_value: very exposed 4th class (some rate it low 5th)
results.evidence: A survey trip report of both summits describes the SW summit as a very exposed 4th-class scramble that some climbers rate low 5th, about 1,500 ft from the NE summit; an independent trip report calls it an exposed class 4 climb. This matches the row's baseFinding and hazards ('fourth class'), so watch_out's flat 'low-5th-class' is corrected.

patches.find: a distinctly harder, more exposed low-5th-class climb
patches.replace: a distinctly harder, very exposed 4th-class climb

results.fact: Total elevation gain — three disagreeing figures
results.evidence: Summit 8,538 ft and Aasgard Pass 7,841 ft are confirmed, with the upper basin around 7,500 ft; from a ~3,400 ft trailhead that puts cumulative round-trip gain near 5,700-6,700 ft depending on camp height, so gain_ft 7,250 looks high and the approach's '5,138-ft round trip' is really the net trailhead-to-summit difference. A survey report gives ~16 mi round trip from Stuart Lake TH (matching the itinerary's 16.6 mi) but no source states a cumulative gain for this itinerary, so no value is adopted.

results.correct_value: Back at camp ~12:30 PM (5.5 hr day)
results.evidence: itinerary.days[1].hours, timing.summitTimeHrs, the sectionBreakdown Climb entry (all 5.5) and timing.totalHrs (7.5+5.5+6.5=19.5) agree against the schedule's 2:00 PM return. A trip report timed Aasgard Pass to the summit at about 2.5 hours, consistent with a ~4-hour camp-to-summit round trip plus margin inside 5.5 hours.
